claim: From 1 July 2027, capital gains will be subject to a new minimum 30% tax rate on all gains.
short_explanation: The 30% minimum rate applies to real capital gains after inflation indexation, not nominal gains. This means the effective tax rate on nominal gains may be substantially lower depending on inflation and the holding period.
detailed_explanation: The headline '30% minimum tax on capital gains' can be misleading. The 30% floor rate applies to actual economic gains after accounting for inflation through indexation, not the nominal gain amount. For example, a $100,000 nominal gain might only be a $40,000 real gain after inflation adjustment, meaning tax would be 30% of $40,000 rather than $100,000. The effective tax rate on nominal gains can be significantly lower than 30% depending on inflation and how long the asset was held.
